subject: ent
title: Complications of otitis media

steps.tx: **Key point.** Middle ear infection spreads beyond its box by direct bone erosion, thrombophlebitic veins or preformed pathways into mastoid, labyrinth, meninges, brain and sigmoid sinus. Antibiotics reduced but never abolished these complications, and chronic cholesteatoma erodes silently toward them. Any ear infection with headache, fever persistence, swelling or neurology is complicated until assessed.
steps.say: Ear infection escaping its box threatens mastoid, brain and venous sinuses. Headache, swelling or neurology with ear disease means complication until checked.

steps.tx: **Acute mastoiditis** follows otitis media when pus fills mastoid air cells and erodes their septa: postauricular swelling pushes the pinna forward and down, with fever and mastoid tenderness. Subperiosteal abscess fluctuates behind the ear; Bezold abscess tracks into the neck. CT confirms coalescent mastoiditis; drainage plus mastoid surgery treats abscess or intracranial extension.
steps.say: Mastoiditis swells behind the ear pushing pinna out. Abscess or brain spread needs drainage and mastoid surgery.

steps.tx: Intracranial spread causes **meningitis** (commonest intracranial complication), extradural and subdural empyema, and temporal lobe or cerebellar **brain abscess** classically with headache, fever, seizures or focal signs and a swinging course. Otogenic abscesses often grow mixed anaerobes and gram negatives. Neurosurgical drainage plus ear surgery and prolonged antibiotics are combined.
steps.say: Ear brain abscesses hide in temporal lobe and cerebellum with headache and seizures. Drain brain and ear together with long antibiotics.

steps.tx: **Lateral (sigmoid) sinus thrombophlebitis** seeds picket fence swinging fevers with rigors as infected clot showers the bloodstream, plus papilloedema from venous hypertension. Gradenigo syndrome combines otorrhoea, retro-orbital pain (trigeminal) and abducens palsy from petrous apex inflammation. Labyrinthitis and facial palsy complete the classic complication catalogue tested repeatedly.
steps.say: Swinging rigors with ear disease mean infected sinus clot. Eye pain plus double vision plus discharging ear means Gradenigo at the petrous tip.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Facial nerve traverses the middle ear and mastoid, so infection or cholesteatoma paralyses it; labyrinthine fistula gives vertigo on pressure. Management principles never change: image urgently, start broad antibiotics per protocol, involve ENT and neurosurgery, and operate the ear source once the patient is stabilised. Lumbar puncture waits for imaging when abscess or raised pressure is possible.
steps.say: Facial palsy or pressure vertigo with ear disease signals nerve or labyrinth breach. Scan first, puncture later when pressure threatens.
